text:
Marta: Quick thread 10am ask: we need a 1-page "inbound flightpath" battlecard for the launch. Audience: infra architects + procurement. Keep to micro-claims + routing play.
Ethan: I can draft. Thinking of a short opener metaphor: "Redwood is air traffic control for models" 1 explains routing, predictability, fallback.
Claire: Love the metaphor. For micro-claims, propose: 1) predictable latency under reserved capacity (cite 30d p99), 2) stable unit economics via batching/caching (link to cost explainer), 3) deployment parity: same API hosted -> VPC -> on-prem.
Noah: For the p99 number let's use a cautious figure: 30d p99 ~ 130ms at seq=512 on dedicated pools. Ops confirm?
salesops-bot: Confirmed: snapshot ms-2026-1809 p99=130ms, median=125ms. Dashboard links posted to #eng-metrics.
Ethan: OK will phrase as "consistent p99 ~130ms on reserved pools (30d)". Footnote with snapshot link. Avoid direct "% faster" claims.
Marta: Rebut bullets vs managed cloud endpoints: 1) "burst = peak, not SLA" 2) "catalog access != production serving guarantees" 3) "onboarding cost matters". Keep them one liner each.
Claire: Add a tiny ops blurb on graceful degradation: "automatic fallback to quantized variants + cross-region failover to maintain SLA". No deep tech in the visible copy, put details in a footnote.
Noah: Inbound routing play: form tags -> enterprise, capacity-sensitive, compliance. Mapping: enterprise+capacity -> AE + solutions eng; compliance -> privacy team + sales ops; others -> self-serve. Provide exact tag strings to sales ops.
Ethan: Draft bullets will include CTA mapping: "Schedule predictable pilot" for enterprise leads, "Start free trial" for self-serve. Also include a 1-sentence customer snippet: "SaaS checkout latency cut from 600ms -> 320ms with reserved capacity and batching" (internal case, anonymized).
Marta: That case sounds good. Make sure it's anonymized and we can cite an internal ticket. Claire, can you confirm the anonymization?
Claire: Confirmed. Use ticket INT-4521 as source footnote.
Noah: Sales ops needs the exact form field names by EOB so they can wire the fast-path. I'll add them to the draft.
salesops-bot: Suggested form fields: `lead_tier`, `capacity_flag`, `compliance_needs`. PR template for form repo: https://git.redwood/forms/pull/123
Ethan: I'll post the first-pass one-pager in the marketing repo at /marketing/webinar-assets/inbound-flightpath-draft.md and tag everyone. Review cycle: 2 rounds, finalize before speaker rehearsal.
Marta: Quick tone note: keep visible copy customer-facing, swap jargon like "KV cache" for "response caching". Technical folks can find details in the footnote.
Claire: I'll add the footnotes: perf snapshot, cost explainer, anonymized case ticket, canary policy link.
Noah: I'll follow up with sales ops to confirm routing SLAs for enterprise handoffs.
Marta: Great. Volunteers to proof? Ethan then Claire for accuracy, Noah for routing. Thanks!
